history.period: Late 18th century (deity tradition c. 1779; temple structure date UNVERIFIED)
history.summary: Shree Shree Bijoy Govindajee Temple is a Vaishnavite temple at Sagolband (Sagalband), Imphal West, distinct from seq 639's royal Shree Govindajee Temple near the palace (similar names; commonly confused). Per ISKCON chroniclers, it received the FIRST of seven deities carved from the sacred Kaina jackfruit tree by King Bhagya Chandra (Jai Singh, r. 1759-1799): after a dream-instruction from Krishna, the king had the tree floated down the Iril River to Langthaban; the first image, named Sri Vijaya Govindaji, was opulently installed at this Sagolband temple (the other six went to Ningthoukhong, Khwai Lamabam, Oinam Thingel, Navadvipa, Lamangdong and the final Govindaji now at the palace temple). The temple building's own founding date is UNVERIFIED; the deity's installation tradition dates to c. 1779.

name: Shree Shree Bijoy Govindajee Temple
town_description: Imphal is the capital of Manipur, set in the flat Imphal Valley at about 786 m and ringed by hills. It is the historic seat of the Meitei kings — Kangla Fort, the former royal palace and the Govindajee temple stand at its centre — and the heart of Manipuri Vaishnavite culture, classical dance and handloom. The city is Manipur's road and air hub, served by Bir Tikendrajit International Airport and national highways to Nagaland, Assam and Myanmar.
